This PR remaps all Babel ast nodes to the original sourcemap location if there's a sourcemap available.

This is an alternative solution to #5831

Performance wise this will likely get even faster after the sourcemap rewrite as the searching of mappings is currently very sub-optimal.

issue_context.title: Parcel 2 forgets to use external sourcemap file (regression)
issue_context.body:
# 🐛 bug report

Setup (app/lib) similar to this closed issue: #4699
When parcel imports library with its own sourcemap it correctly uses sourcemap on load but then on executing code (e.g. button click) it points to (correct) line in bundle index file instead.

This works fine in versions up to 2.0.0-nightly.520.

It breaks in versions => 2.0.0-nightly.522

## 🎛 Configuration (.babelrc, package.json, cli command)

<!--- If describing a bug, tell us what your babel configuration looks like -->

## 🤔 Expected Behavior

Should provide link/address to individual file.
<!--- Tell us what should happen -->

## 😯 Current Behavior

It links to index.xxxxx.js (bundled file) instead

## 💁 Possible Solution

<!--- Not obligatory, but suggest a fix/reason for the bug -->

## 🔦 Context

<!--- How has this issue affected you? What are you trying to accomplish? -->

<!--- Providing context helps us come up with a solution that is most useful in the real world -->

## 💻 Code Sample

<!-- Please provide a code repository, gist, code snippet or sample files to reproduce the issue -->

## 🌍 Your Environment

<!--- Include as many relevant details about the environment you experienced the bug in -->

| Software         | Version(s) |
| ---------------- | ---------- |
| Parcel           | 2.0.0-nightly.522
| Node             | 14.5.0
| npm/Yarn         | 6.14.5
| Operating System | Windows 10

<!-- Love parcel? Please consider supporting our collective:
👉  https://opencollective.com/parcel/donate -->
comments:
Small reproduction: https://github.com/mischnic/parcel-issue-5620

Seems to only happen with the Rollup umd build, not CJS / ESM builds: https://github.com/mischnic/parcel-issue-5620/blob/master/app-src/index.js

cc @DeMoorJasper
Thanks @mischnic for checking it. I confirm in my real app I am using umd which fits your observation.

I think I'm encountering this bug.  I noticed after doing an npm update this morning, browser debugging doesn't work correctly because references to lines of source code are wrong.  Disabling sourcemaps in developer-tools is a temporary work-around for me.
@ebrensi what version of parcel have you got installed? After updating packages you may want to try deleting `.parcel-cache` folder and possibly your previous output files. Then run parcel again.

@gregid I'm running 2.0.0-nightly.524.  It turns out disabling sourcemaps is not a fix.  I have tried doing a full clean of cached and previously built files.  It does not help and in fact appears to be stuck using a piece of source code that I have since changed.
@ebrensi one more suggestion from me - `ctrl + f5`/`closing browser`/`cleaning web browser cache` helped me few times in similar situation with parcel

It seems to have come from doing an `npm audit fix`.   I normally specify `next` for Parcel version in my `package.json` but npm complains that there are a lot of security vulnerabilities and suggests I perform an `npm audit fix`.  So I did that.  I am not sure what changes were made except that the version of Parcel in my `package.json` was updated from `next` to `2.0.0-nightly.524`, and debugging in Chrome developer tools becomes difficult because the lines of code being pointed to are wrong, for example when attempting to set a break point or step through the source code.  I presume this is a problem with the sourcemaps.  I was able to get it working again by changing the Parcel version back to `next` in `package.json`, wiping my `node_modules` folder and re-`npm install`-ing, but then npm complains about 46 vulnerabilities again.
@ebrensi I think it needs to be put in a separate issue as it is clear now these two are separate problems - you will also have greater chance parcel developers will address the issue.

I think I'm finding the same problem when going from 2.0.0-beta.1 to 2.0.0-beta.2, eith nothing else changing the sourcemaps are not available on Chrome.
Going back to 2.0.0-beta.1 makes them available again.

review_comments: Should this be getSourceContent rather than plural? Or even just getSource? We'd have getCode which gets the compiled code and getSource which gets the source code?
but it can return multiple sources? (in case of a bundled library)
I'm probably forgetting something but why do runtimes need a source map that is just 1:1 with the code again?
To have the source content and in case we do transformations on the runtime
Ah because it's not actually on disk. Got it

This is a bit hacky, but the alternative I've thought of isn't much better and probably slower which is using the mapping after the found mapping to get the end position.

This would also not be a lot more accurate as sourcemaps don't really capture as much nodes as babel does and therefore might not be the actual end
We should make sure that this doesn't end up stored in the graph...
Maybe runtimes shouldn't return a filePath but a directory? Otherwise people might be confused that the asset doesn't actually use the filePath they specify?
for the sourcemap we do need some filepath, not sure what we should do for the actual asset it returns though. This PR does not (need) to touch this though
Yeah I mean core would still add a filename but plugins would only return a dir. right now they return a file but the filename part isn't used
So we should just make core append `/index` or something to the dirname as filename? Maybe out of scope for this PR?
